status_changes.description: PASS must be sent after USER command for authentication
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites specific session observations (Sessions 1-8, 10) showing USER followed by 331, then PASS. This is direct observational evidence from traces.

status_changes.description: Data transfer commands (LIST, RETR, STOR, NLST) require successful authentication (USER/PASS sequence completing with 230)
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites specific trace observations: 'All data transfers in traces occur after successful PASS response 230' and references Session 6 failure/retry pattern.

status_changes.description: PASV or PORT should be sent before data transfer commands to establish data connection
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites Session 4 showing PASV -> 227 before LIST/STOR. While it notes other sessions may use active mode, the claim is supported by observed behavior in at least one session.

status_changes.description: QUIT can be sent from any state to terminate session
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites Session 9 where QUIT was sent immediately after connection (RESP_220), and notes all sessions end with QUIT. This supports the 'any state' claim.

status_changes.description: After authentication failure (PASS returns 530), user may retry with USER command
status_changes.rationale: Evidence explicitly cites Session 2 and Session 6 showing PASS -> 530 followed by USER -> 331, PASS -> 230. Direct trace evidence.

status_changes.description: RNTO must follow RNFR command for rename operations
status_changes.rationale: Evidence relies on 'Standard FTP rename protocol' documentation rather than direct trace observation of the sequence in the provided sessions. While likely true, it lacks specific session trace citation.

status_changes.description: Initial server greeting (220) is received before any client commands
status_changes.rationale: Evidence states 'All sessions start with RESP_220 -> 220 before any client command'. This is a strong universal claim backed by observation of all sessions.

status_changes.description: TYPE command can be sent after authentication to set transfer mode before data transfers
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites specific sessions: Session 3 (TYPE before RETR) and Session 7 (TYPE before STOR). Direct observational evidence.

status_changes.description: FEAT command is typically sent after authentication to discover server capabilities
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites Session 5 showing FEAT sent after successful PASS. The word 'typically' makes the claim conservative enough to be supported by single-session evidence.

status_changes.description: SYST command is typically sent after authentication to query server OS type
status_changes.rationale: Evidence cites Session 3 showing SYST sent after successful authentication. The word 'typically' makes the claim conservative enough to be supported by single-session evidence.
